question: What is the school bus "danger zone"?
choice_a: The area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit, either by another vehicle or their own bus
choice_b: Only the area directly behind the bus where the stop arm is located
choice_c: Only the area visible through the overhead rearview mirror
choice_d: The area inside the bus near the emergency exits
explanation: The manual defines the danger zone as the area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit by another vehicle or the bus itself.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: How far can the danger zone extend in front of the school bus, and which part of it is the most dangerous?
choice_a: It extends 10 feet, with the last 2 feet being most dangerous
choice_b: It can extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_c: It extends 50 feet, with the middle 20 feet being most dangerous
choice_d: It extends only to the edge of the front bumper
explanation: The danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: How far do the danger zones extend from the left and right sides of the school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 20 feet
choice_c: 10 feet
choice_d: 15 feet
explanation: The danger zones extend 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: How far behind the rear bumper of the school bus does the danger zone extend?
choice_a: 20 feet
choice_b: 5 feet
choice_c: 15 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: The danger zone extends 10 feet behind the rear bumper of the school bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Why is the area to the left of the school bus always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because of passing cars
choice_b: Because the emergency exit is located there
choice_c: Because the fuel tank is on that side
choice_d: Because the driver cannot see that side at all
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Why is proper adjustment and use of all mirrors described as vital to safe school bus operation?
choice_a: It improves fuel economy
choice_b: In order to observe the danger zone around the bus and look for students, traffic, and other objects in that area
choice_c: It is required only for the post-trip inspection
choice_d: It automatically activates the stop signal arm
explanation: Proper mirror adjustment and use is vital so the driver can observe the danger zone and watch for students, traffic, and other objects.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.2 Correct Mirror Adjustment

question: When should a school bus driver check each mirror to obtain maximum viewing area?
choice_a: Only once a week during scheduled maintenance
choice_b: Only after an accident
choice_c: Always, before operating the school bus
choice_d: Only if a passenger complains
explanation: The manual states drivers should always check each mirror before operating the school bus to obtain maximum viewing area.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.2 Correct Mirror Adjustment

question: Where are the outside left and right side flat mirrors mounted, and what do they help the driver monitor?
choice_a: On the rear bumper, to monitor tire pressure
choice_b: Inside the bus above the aisle, to monitor student seating
choice_c: Below the convex mirrors, to monitor the engine
choice_d: At the left and right front corners of the bus, to monitor traffic, check clearances, and watch students on the sides and rear of the bus
explanation: The outside flat mirrors are mounted at the left and right front corners of the bus and are used to monitor traffic, check clearances, and watch students on the sides and to the rear of the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: When the outside flat mirrors are properly adjusted, how far behind the bus should the driver be able to see?
choice_a: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_b: 50 feet or 1 bus length behind the bus
choice_c: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths behind the bus
choice_d: 300 feet or 6 bus lengths behind the bus
explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should allow the driver to see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: Besides the distance behind the bus, what else should the outside flat mirrors show when properly adjusted?
choice_a: Only the interior aisle
choice_b: Along the sides of the bus and the rear tires touching the ground
choice_c: Only the front bumper
choice_d: Only the engine compartment
explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should also show along the sides of the bus and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located?
choice_a: Above the windshield
choice_b: At the rear of the bus
choice_c: Below the outside flat mirrors
choice_d: On the interior dashboard
explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors and are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: What is an important characteristic of the view provided by the convex mirrors?
choice_a: They only work at night
choice_b: They show the exact size and distance of people and objects
choice_c: They eliminate all blind spots on the bus
choice_d: They present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus
explanation: The manual warns that convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: When properly positioned, what should the convex mirrors allow the driver to see, in addition to at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus?
choice_a: Front of the rear tires touching the ground
choice_b: The stop signal arm
choice_c: The overhead rearview mirror
choice_d: The interior of the bus
explanation: Convex mirrors should be positioned to see the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: Where are the left and right side crossover mirrors mounted?
choice_a: At the rear bumper
choice_b: On both the left and right front corners of the bus
choice_c: Above the driver's seat
choice_d: Inside the bus near the emergency door
explanation: The crossover mirrors are mounted on both the left and right front corners of the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: What area do the crossover mirrors let the driver see that is not visible by direct vision?
choice_a: The rear window of the bus
choice_b: The engine compartment
choice_c: The front bumper "danger zone" area directly in front of the bus
choice_d: The interior aisle of the bus
explanation: Crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: Besides the left side danger zone, what other area on the right side do the crossover mirrors show?
choice_a: The rear axle
choice_b: The service door and front wheel area
choice_c: The exhaust system
choice_d: The stop signal arm
explanation: Crossover mirrors view the danger zone area to the left side and the right side of the bus, including the service door and front wheel area.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: When the crossover mirrors are properly adjusted, what should overlap in the area from the front bumper to the point where direct vision is possible?
choice_a: Direct vision and mirror view vision
choice_b: The convex and overhead mirrors
choice_c: The interior and exterior lighting
choice_d: The flat mirror and the dome light
explanation: The manual states direct vision and mirror view vision should overlap for the area in front of the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror mounted?
choice_a: Directly above the windshield on the driver's side area of the bus
choice_b: On the exterior rear of the bus
choice_c: Below the dashboard
choice_d: On the crossover mirror bracket
explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side area of the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: What is the overhead inside rearview mirror primarily used for?
choice_a: Checking tire pressure
choice_b: Monitoring passenger activity inside the bus
choice_c: Watching for oncoming trains
choice_d: Viewing the front danger zone
explanation: This mirror is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: The overhead inside rearview mirror may provide limited visibility directly behind the bus if the bus is equipped with what?
choice_a: A backup camera
choice_b: An extra set of convex mirrors
choice_c: Tinted rear windows
choice_d: A glass-bottomed rear emergency door
explanation: The overhead mirror may provide limited visibility directly behind the bus if it is equipped with a glass-bottomed rear emergency door.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: Because of the large blind spot beginning at the rear bumper that could extend up to 400 feet or more, what must the driver use to monitor that area?
choice_a: The exterior side mirrors
choice_b: The overhead mirror alone
choice_c: The dome light
choice_d: The convex mirrors alone
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to use the exterior side mirrors to monitor traffic that approaches and enters the large blind spot area extending up to 400 feet or more behind the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: Can a school bus driver change the location of a bus stop on their own?
choice_a: Yes, anytime it is more convenient
choice_b: No, never without written approval from the appropriate school district official
choice_c: Yes, but only during bad weather
choice_d: Yes, if the driver is running late
explanation: The manual states a driver should never change the location of a bus stop without written approval from the appropriate school district official.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: How should a driver approach a school bus stop?
choice_a: At normal highway speed
choice_b: While sounding the horn continuously
choice_c: Cautiously, at a slow rate of speed
choice_d: With high beams activated at all times
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to approach the stop cautiously at a slow rate of speed.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: If the bus is so equipped, when should the alternating flashing amber warning lights be activated when approaching a stop?
choice_a: Only after the bus has fully stopped
choice_b: At least 500 feet or 15 seconds before the stop
choice_c: At least 50 feet or 1-2 seconds before the stop
choice_d: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the stop, or in accordance with state law
explanation: The manual states alternating flashing amber warning lights should be activated at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: About how far, or how many seconds, before pulling over should the driver turn on the right turn signal indicator?
choice_a: About 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over
choice_b: About 500-600 feet or 20 seconds before pulling over
choice_c: Immediately at the moment of stopping
choice_d: About 20 feet or less than 1 second before pulling over
explanation: The right turn signal indicator should be turned on about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When bringing the school bus to a full stop at a designated stop, how far away should the front bumper be from students, and why?
choice_a: Right next to the students, so they do not need to walk
choice_b: At least 10 feet away, which forces students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements
choice_c: At least 2 feet away, for a quicker loading process
choice_d: At least 25 feet away, to save fuel
explanation: The bus should stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students; this forces students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: What final check should the driver make before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach?
choice_a: Check the fuel gauge
choice_b: Check the interior dome light only
choice_c: Make a final check to see that all traffic has stopped
choice_d: Honk the horn once
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to make a final check that all traffic has stopped before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When should students board the school bus?
choice_a: As soon as the bus comes into view
choice_b: As soon as the amber warning lights begin flashing
choice_c: As soon as the door opens
choice_d: Only when signaled by the driver
explanation: Students should board the bus only when signaled by the driver.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: If there is a student missing at a stop while counting students boarding, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Ask the other students where the missing student is
choice_b: Leave immediately and report it after the route
choice_c: Drive around the block to search
choice_d: Call the police before checking with other students
explanation: If a student is missing, the driver should ask the other students where the student is.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: How should students board the school bus?
choice_a: Two at a time, side by side
choice_b: Slowly, in single file, and using the handrail
choice_c: Quickly, in any order
choice_d: Running to avoid delaying the route
explanation: Students should board slowly, in single file, and use the handrail.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: Before moving the bus after loading students, what should the driver wait for?
choice_a: The dispatcher to give clearance
choice_b: Exactly two minutes to pass
choice_c: Students to be seated and facing forward
choice_d: Every student to fasten a seatbelt and raise a hand
explanation: The driver should wait until students are seated and facing forward before moving the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: If the driver cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Sound the horn repeatedly and drive away
choice_b: Wait exactly five minutes before acting
choice_c: Radio dispatch and continue the route
choice_d: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
explanation: If a student outside the bus cannot be accounted for, the driver should secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: What should the driver do while students are unloading, to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop?
choice_a: Turn off the interior lights
choice_b: Radio the school office
choice_c: Open all bus windows
choice_d: Count the number of students while unloading
explanation: The driver should count the number of students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: After exiting the bus during a route unloading stop, how far should students walk away from the side of the bus so the driver can plainly see them?
choice_a: 2 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: Students should exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: What does the manual instruct a driver to do if they have missed a student's unloading stop?
choice_a: Do not back up; be sure to follow local procedures
choice_b: Back up carefully to the stop
choice_c: Continue and return to the stop at the end of the route without further guidance
choice_d: Call the student's parents to arrange pickup elsewhere
explanation: If a driver has missed a student's unloading stop, the manual says do not back up and to follow local procedures.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, where should the student walk to next, after first moving 10 feet away from the side of the bus?
choice_a: Directly behind the bus
choice_b: Into the roadway immediately
choice_c: The opposite side of the road without stopping
choice_d: A location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus
explanation: Students crossing the roadway should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, remaining away from the front of the school bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When students reach the edge of the roadway before crossing, what are they supposed to do?
choice_a: Stop and look in all directions, making sure the roadway is clear and safe, and wait for the driver's signal
choice_b: Proceed to cross immediately without stopping
choice_c: Run across quickly before traffic arrives
choice_d: Wave to the driver and continue walking
explanation: At the edge of the roadway, students should stop, look in all directions to make sure it is clear and safe, check the flashing red lights, and wait for the driver's signal before crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When unloading at the school, how should the driver secure the bus after performing a safe stop?
choice_a: Leave the engine running with the doors open
choice_b: Leave the key in the ignition for a quick departure
choice_c: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_d: Set only the parking brake and leave the engine on
explanation: When unloading at school, the driver secures the bus by turning off the ignition switch and removing the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: While unloading at school, in what manner should students exit the bus?
choice_a: All at once
choice_b: By grade level only
choice_c: Running to reach the school entrance faster
choice_d: An orderly fashion
explanation: The manual instructs that students should have students exit in an orderly fashion when unloading at school.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: After unloading at school, why should the driver walk through the bus?
choice_a: To collect trash left on the bus
choice_b: To check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students
choice_c: To test the emergency exits for the day
choice_d: To check the fuel level before the next trip
explanation: The driver should walk through the bus to check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

question: If the driver cannot account for a student outside the bus after unloading at school and the bus is secure, what should be done?
choice_a: Leave the area immediately
choice_b: Contact only the police and take no other action
choice_c: Do nothing further since the bus is secure
choice_d: Check around and underneath the bus
explanation: If a student cannot be accounted for and the bus is secure, the driver should check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What special danger is created if a student drops an object near the bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: It may cause a flat tire
choice_b: Stopping or returning to pick up the object may cause the student to disappear from the driver's sight at a very dangerous moment
choice_c: It will trigger the stop arm to retract automatically
choice_d: It will set off the alarm system
explanation: Stopping to pick up a dropped object, or returning to pick it up, may cause the student to disappear from the driver's sight at a very dangerous moment.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What should students be told to do if they drop an object near the bus?
choice_a: Pick it up immediately no matter the circumstances
choice_b: Wait exactly where they are until the object is retrieved by an adult
choice_c: Leave the object, move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, and try to get the driver's attention to retrieve it
choice_d: Ask the nearest passing car for help
explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, attempting to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: According to the "Handrail Hang-ups" warning, what has caused injury or death to students exiting a school bus?
choice_a: Icy pavement near the bus
choice_b: Low interior lighting
choice_c: Overcrowding in the aisle
choice_d: Clothing, accessories, or even parts of their body getting caught in the handrail or door as they exited
explanation: The manual warns students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or body parts got caught in the handrail or door as they exited the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: When should a driver conduct a post-trip inspection of the bus?
choice_a: Only before the morning route begins
choice_b: When the route or school activity trip is finished
choice_c: Only once per week
choice_d: Only if instructed by dispatch that day
explanation: The manual states a post-trip inspection should be conducted when the route or school activity trip is finished.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: During the post-trip inspection, the driver should walk through and around the bus looking for which of the following, with special attention to items unique to school buses?
choice_a: Fuel receipts and toll records
choice_b: Articles left on the bus, sleeping students, and mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
choice_c: Only tire tread depth
choice_d: Only the maintenance log book
explanation: The post-trip inspection includes looking for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows/doors, and mechanical or operational problems, with special attention to mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: Any problems or special situations found during the post-trip inspection should be reported to whom?
choice_a: The next scheduled driver only
choice_b: The students' parents
choice_c: Your supervisor or school authorities immediately
choice_d: The local police department only
explanation: Problems or special situations found during the post-trip inspection should be reported immediately to your supervisor or school authorities.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: What is the first and most important consideration when determining whether to evacuate a school bus?
choice_a: Contacting the students' parents
choice_b: Checking the bus's fuel level
choice_c: Waiting for law enforcement to arrive
choice_d: Recognizing the hazard
explanation: The first and most important consideration is for the driver to recognize the hazard.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: If time permits, what should a school bus driver do before deciding to evacuate the bus?
choice_a: Contact their dispatcher to explain the situation
choice_b: Evacuate immediately regardless of the situation
choice_c: Ask the students for a vote
choice_d: Wait ten minutes to reassess
explanation: If time permits, school bus drivers should contact their dispatcher to explain the situation before making a decision to evacuate.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: As a general rule, how is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk?
choice_a: By immediately evacuating all students
choice_b: By keeping students on the bus
choice_c: By opening all bus windows
choice_d: By calling a substitute driver to take over
explanation: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition to consider when deciding whether to evacuate the bus?
choice_a: Whether the route is running behind schedule
choice_b: Whether students have their backpacks
choice_c: Whether the two-way radio has a full battery
choice_d: Whether there is a fire or danger of fire
explanation: One of the listed conditions to consider is whether there is a fire or danger of fire.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: The manual lists "would moving students complicate injuries" as a consideration for evacuation. What specific types of injuries are mentioned?
choice_a: Sunburn and dehydration
choice_b: Neck and back injuries and fractures
choice_c: Common colds and allergies
choice_d: Minor bruises only
explanation: The manual specifically raises whether moving students would complicate injuries such as neck and back injuries and fractures.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition requiring MANDATORY evacuation of the bus?
choice_a: The bus is on fire or there is a threat of a fire
choice_b: The route is running ten minutes late
choice_c: A tire has low pressure
choice_d: A student has misplaced their backpack
explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when it is on fire or there is a threat of a fire, per the mandatory evacuation conditions.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Besides fire, which of these is also listed as a mandatory evacuation condition?
choice_a: Low fuel level
choice_b: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_c: A malfunctioning radio
choice_d: A missed turn on the route
explanation: Mandatory evacuation is also required when the bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: When possible, how many responsible, older student assistants should be assigned to each emergency exit?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Four
explanation: When possible, drivers should assign two responsible, older student assistants to each emergency exit.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: Because there may not be older, responsible students on the bus at the time of an emergency, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Rely solely on the intercom system
choice_b: Skip any evacuation planning
choice_c: Only inform the front-row students of the procedures
choice_d: Explain emergency evacuation procedures to all students
explanation: Since there may not be older, responsible students available, emergency evacuation procedures must be explained to all students.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: How far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic, should a "safe place" generally be, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus?
choice_a: At least 100 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: A safe place should be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If fire is present during a bus evacuation, in which direction should students be led?
choice_a: Directly toward the fire to assess it
choice_b: Upwind of the bus
choice_c: Downwind of the bus
choice_d: Directly behind the bus
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to lead students upwind of the bus if fire is present.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: When evacuating near railroad tracks, in which direction should students be led, and how far from the tracks?
choice_a: Toward the tracks, to move away from traffic
choice_b: Parallel to the tracks in either direction
choice_c: As far away from the tracks as possible, in the direction of any oncoming train
choice_d: Toward the nearest crossing signal box
explanation: Students should be led as far away from railroad tracks as possible and in the direction of any oncoming train.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, how far upwind should the driver lead students?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 200 feet
choice_c: At least 300 feet
choice_d: 500 feet
explanation: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and evacuation is ordered, and shelter in a building is not readily available, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert and direct them to lie face down, hands covering their head
choice_b: Keep everyone seated with seatbelts fastened
choice_c: Drive toward the nearest overpass for shelter
choice_d: Lead students to stand in an open field
explanation: If shelter in a building is not readily available, the driver should escort students to a nearby ditch or culvert and direct them to lie face down with hands covering their head.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: When securing the bus prior to evacuation, in addition to setting the parking brakes and shutting off the engine, what else should be done?
choice_a: Leave the radio on for updates
choice_b: Remove the ignition key and activate hazard-warning lights
choice_c: Leave the headlights on
choice_d: Leave the ignition key in place for later use
explanation: Securing the bus includes removing the ignition key and activating the hazard-warning lights.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What does the manual instruct regarding a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury during an evacuation?
choice_a: Move them immediately to the safe place regardless of circumstances
choice_b: Leave them completely unattended until help arrives
choice_c: Do not move them unless their life is in immediate danger
choice_d: Always move them first, before any other students
explanation: The manual states not to move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If no radio is available or the radio is inoperable, who should the driver dispatch to call for help, and who is the last resort?
choice_a: A student should always go first, followed by a passing motorist
choice_b: The driver should personally go for help, leaving the students behind
choice_c: No one should be dispatched under any circumstances
choice_d: Dispatch a passing motorist or area resident first; as a last resort, dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help
explanation: If the radio is unavailable or inoperable, the driver should dispatch a passing motorist or area resident to call for help; as a last resort, two older, responsible students may be dispatched.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: After evacuating students, what should the driver do to ensure no students remain on the bus, and what should be retrieved?
choice_a: Walk through the bus to ensure no students remain, and retrieve emergency equipment
choice_b: Call dispatch and wait outside without checking the bus
choice_c: Count heads from a distance only
choice_d: Trust the student assistants' report without checking personally
explanation: The driver should walk through the bus to ensure no students remain on the bus and retrieve emergency equipment.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What characterizes a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has flashing red lights and bells
choice_b: It does not have any type of traffic control device
choice_c: It is found only on interstate highways
choice_d: It always has a gate
explanation: A passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: At a passive railroad-highway crossing, in whose hands does the decision to proceed rest?
choice_a: The train conductor
choice_b: A crossing guard
choice_c: Entirely in the driver's hands
choice_d: The school district transportation office
explanation: At passive crossings, the decision to proceed rests entirely in the driver's hands.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: Which devices help a driver recognize a passive crossing?
choice_a: Gates and bells only
choice_b: A traffic light
choice_c: A police checkpoint sign
choice_d: Yellow circular advance warning signs, pavement markings, and cross-bucks
explanation: Passive crossings have yellow circular advance warning signs, pavement markings, and cross-bucks to assist drivers in recognizing the crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: What characterizes an "active" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, such as flashing red lights with or without bells, or flashing red lights with bells and gates
choice_b: It has no signage of any kind
choice_c: It relies entirely on the driver's judgment with no devices
choice_d: It is marked only by a yellow circular sign
explanation: An active crossing has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights with or without bells and flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: What shape and color is the advance warning sign placed ahead of a public railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: Square, red-on-white
choice_b: Round, black-on-yellow
choice_c: Triangular, orange
choice_d: Octagonal, red
explanation: The round, black-on-yellow warning sign is placed ahead of a public railroad-highway crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: What does the advance warning sign tell a driver to do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the crossing before the train arrives
choice_b: Ignore it unless a train is visibly present
choice_c: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously through the crossing
explanation: The advance warning sign tells the driver to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: What do the pavement markings at a railroad crossing consist of, and where must the front of the school bus remain if there is a white stop line?
choice_a: A yield triangle; the bus must stop past the line
choice_b: Double yellow lines; the line does not apply to buses
choice_c: An "X" with the letters "RR" and a no-passing marking; the front of the bus must remain behind the stop line
choice_d: A stop hexagon painted on the road; position does not matter
explanation: Pavement markings consist of an X with the letters RR and a no-passing marking; the front of the school bus must remain behind the white stop line while stopped at the crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: What does the cross-buck sign require the driver to do, and where must the bus stop if there is no white line painted on the pavement?
choice_a: Yield the right-of-way to the train; stop before the cross-buck sign
choice_b: Proceed without stopping; no stop is required
choice_c: Slow to 15 mph only; stopping is optional
choice_d: Activate the stop arm; stop at the advance warning sign
explanation: The cross-buck sign requires the driver to yield the right-of-way to the train; if there is no white line painted on the pavement, the driver must stop the bus before the cross-buck sign.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: When flashing red light signals begin to flash at a crossing, and there is more than one track, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Proceed slowly since bells are only advisory
choice_b: Stop, yield the right-of-way to the train, and make sure all tracks are clear before crossing
choice_c: Accelerate through before the gate lowers
choice_d: Wait exactly 30 seconds then proceed regardless of the tracks
explanation: When the lights begin to flash, the driver must stop and yield the right-of-way to the train; if there is more than one track, the driver must make sure all tracks are clear before crossing.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: At a gated crossing, when should the driver stop, and what should be done if the gate stays down after the train passes?
choice_a: Stop only after the gate is fully lowered; proceed slowly around the gate
choice_b: There is no need to stop if gates are present
choice_c: Stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers; remain stopped until the gates go up and lights stop flashing; if the gate stays down after the train passes, do not drive around it, instead call the dispatcher
choice_d: Stop only if a police officer signals to do so
explanation: Drivers must stop when lights begin flashing and before the gate lowers, remain stopped until gates rise and lights stop flashing, and if the gate stays down after the train passes, not drive around it but call the dispatcher instead.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: According to the manual, how must school buses generally operate at railroad-highway crossings?
choice_a: They must slow down but are not required to stop unless a train is visible
choice_b: They must stop at all crossings and ensure it is safe before proceeding
choice_c: They must stop only at active crossings
choice_d: They may proceed without stopping if running behind schedule
explanation: In general, school buses must stop at all crossings and ensure it is safe before proceeding across the tracks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: Why does the manual state that a school bus does not have the "slightest edge" when involved in a crash with a train?
choice_a: Because of a train's size and weight it cannot stop quickly, and no emergency escape route exists for a train
choice_b: Because trains always have priority legally, regardless of physics
choice_c: Because school buses lack proper brakes
choice_d: Because trains are always faster than buses
explanation: Because of a train's size and weight, it cannot stop quickly, and an emergency escape route does not exist for a train.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: About how far before a railroad crossing should the driver activate hazard lights while approaching?
choice_a: 50 feet
choice_b: Approximately 200 feet
choice_c: 500 feet
choice_d: 20 feet
explanation: The driver should activate hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make intentions known.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At the crossing, how close and how far should the bus stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet, no farther than 20 feet
choice_b: No closer than 25 feet, no farther than 75 feet
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet, no exceptions
explanation: The driver should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where there is the best view of the tracks.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At the crossing, what should be done with the transmission and brakes?
choice_a: Leave the transmission in Drive with a foot off the brake
choice_b: Rev the engine while in Park
choice_c: Leave the transmission in Reverse for a quick getaway
choice_d: Place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and press down on the service brake or set the parking brakes
explanation: At the crossing, the driver should place the transmission in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and press down on the service brake or set the parking brakes.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: Before opening the service door and driver's window at the crossing to look and listen for an approaching train, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Turn off all radios and noisy equipment, and silence the passengers
choice_b: Turn on the radio to listen for a train alert broadcast
choice_c: Turn on the interior dome light
choice_d: Release the parking brake completely
explanation: The driver should turn off all radios and noisy equipment and silence the passengers before opening the service door and driver's window to look and listen for a train.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should the bus stop, and when should it proceed?
choice_a: Stop between every pair of tracks; proceed after each individual track is confirmed clear
choice_b: Stop only before the first set of tracks; once sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all of the tracks until completely cleared
choice_c: Stop only at the last track before exiting
choice_d: No stop is required if the gates are up
explanation: At a multiple-track crossing, the bus should stop only before the first set of tracks; once sure no train is approaching on any track, the driver should proceed across all tracks until completely cleared.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: In what gear should the bus cross railroad tracks, and what should the driver do if the gate comes down after the bus has already started crossing?
choice_a: Highest gear; stop immediately on the tracks
choice_b: Neutral, coasting across; reverse off the tracks
choice_c: A low gear, without changing gears while crossing; drive through the gate even if it means breaking it
choice_d: Any gear is acceptable; wait for the gate to rise again before continuing
explanation: The bus should cross the tracks in a low gear without changing gears; if the gate comes down after the bus has started across, the driver should drive through it even if it means breaking the gate.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If a school bus stalls or is trapped on railroad tracks, what is the first priority, and in what direction should everyone move?
choice_a: Try to restart the engine repeatedly before doing anything else
choice_b: Wait inside the bus for the crossing signal to stop flashing
choice_c: Call the school district first, then evacuate
choice_d: Get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving at an angle away from the tracks and toward the train
explanation: If the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, everyone must get out and off the tracks immediately, moving away from the bus at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: If there is no police officer at a crossing and the driver believes the crossing signal is malfunctioning, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Call the dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions on how to proceed
choice_b: Proceed immediately since no officer is present to stop them
choice_c: Wait exactly ten minutes then proceed regardless
choice_d: Drive around and report the malfunction after completing the route
explanation: If there is no police officer and the driver believes the signal is malfunctioning, the driver should call the dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: Why should a driver plan a route that provides maximum sight distance at highway-rail grade crossings?
choice_a: So the driver does not attempt to cross the tracks unless able to see far enough to know for certain that no trains are approaching
choice_b: To reduce wear on the brakes
choice_c: It is only a state inspection requirement with no safety purpose
choice_d: To avoid speed bumps on the approach
explanation: Planning the route for maximum sight distance ensures the driver does not attempt to cross the tracks unless able to see far enough to know for certain that no trains are approaching.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: At passive crossings, the manual warns drivers to be especially careful even if nearby active railroad signals indicate the tracks are clear. Why?
choice_a: The driver must still look and listen to be sure it is safe to proceed
choice_b: Active signals at other crossings are always inaccurate
choice_c: Passive crossings never actually have train traffic
choice_d: This warning applies only to non-school vehicles
explanation: Even if active railroad signals indicate the tracks are clear, drivers must still look and listen at passive crossings to be sure it is safe to proceed.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: As a general rule, how many feet should be added to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area on the far side of a crossing?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 20 feet
choice_d: 15 feet
explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area, summarized by the phrase "if it won't fit, don't commit."
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: Why does loading and unloading students require all of the driver's concentration?
choice_a: So the driver can concentrate on the driving task and not take their eyes off what is happening outside the bus
choice_b: To ensure the route stays on time
choice_c: To conserve fuel during idling
choice_d: So the driver can monitor the radio for dispatch calls
explanation: In order to get students to and from school safely and on time, the driver needs to concentrate on the driving task and not take their eyes off what is happening outside the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.1 Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: If there is a behavior problem on the bus while students are unloading, what should the driver do first?
choice_a: Stop the bus immediately mid-unload to address it
choice_b: Wait until the students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away
choice_c: Call the police right away regardless of severity
choice_d: Ignore it until the entire route is finished
explanation: If there is a behavior problem while loading or unloading, the driver should wait until the students unloading are safely off the bus and have moved away.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.1 Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: If necessary to handle a behavior problem after students are safely off the bus, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Continue driving and handle it verbally over the intercom
choice_b: Radio the school and keep driving
choice_c: Pull the bus over to handle the problem
choice_d: Wait until the end of the route regardless of the severity
explanation: If necessary, the driver should pull the bus over to handle a behavior problem.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.1 Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: For discipline or refusal of rights to ride the bus, what should a driver follow?
choice_a: Their own personal judgment exclusively
choice_b: The school's procedures for discipline or refusal of rights to ride the bus
choice_c: State police guidance exclusively
choice_d: No formal procedure is described
explanation: Drivers should follow the school's procedures for discipline or refusal of rights to ride the bus.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: When stopping the bus to handle a serious problem, where should the driver park?
choice_a: In the travel lane with hazard lights on
choice_b: On the shoulder of a high-speed highway
choice_c: In a safe location off the road, perhaps a parking lot or a driveway
choice_d: Wherever is immediately available, regardless of safety
explanation: The driver should stop the bus and park in a safe location off the road, perhaps a parking lot or a driveway.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: If the driver must leave their seat to secure the bus while addressing a serious problem, what should be done?
choice_a: Leave the engine running for convenience
choice_b: Take the ignition key with them
choice_c: Leave the door open for ventilation
choice_d: Do nothing special before leaving the seat
explanation: The driver should secure the bus and take the ignition key with them if leaving their seat.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: How should the driver speak to a student causing a serious problem, and what should the driver avoid showing?
choice_a: Speak respectfully and courteously with a firm voice; avoid showing anger, but show that you mean business
choice_b: Speak loudly to assert authority; avoid showing any calmness
choice_c: Say nothing and use written notes only; avoid eye contact
choice_d: Speak sarcastically to discourage repeat behavior; avoid showing firmness
explanation: The driver should stand up and speak respectfully in a courteous manner with a firm voice, remind the offender of expected behavior, and not show anger, but show that the driver means business.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: If a change of seating is needed for a problem student, what should the driver request?
choice_a: That the student sit alone at the very back
choice_b: That the student move to a seat near the driver
choice_c: That the student get off at the next stop
choice_d: That the student stand for the remainder of the route
explanation: If a change of seating is needed, the driver should request that the student move to a seat near the driver.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: Where is a student allowed to be put off the bus, and what should the driver do if an offense is too serious to safely drive?
choice_a: Anywhere the driver deems appropriate; continue the route regardless
choice_b: Only at the nearest safe pull-off; wait indefinitely without calling anyone
choice_c: Only at school or at his or her designated school bus stop; call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student
choice_d: At any stop if severely disruptive; let another student handle it
explanation: A student may never be put off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop; if the offense is too serious to safely drive, the driver should call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: Air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after what date are required by the Department of Transportation to have antilock braking systems?
choice_a: January 1, 1995
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: June 1, 2000
choice_d: March 1, 2001
explanation: The DOT requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more are required to have ABS if built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: January 1, 1997
choice_c: June 1, 2000
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp found on the instrument panel of a school bus equipped with ABS?
choice_a: Red
choice_b: Green
choice_c: Yellow
choice_d: Blue
explanation: A school bus equipped with ABS will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What can happen to a vehicle's wheels when the driver brakes hard on slippery surfaces without ABS?
choice_a: They automatically release pressure
choice_b: Nothing changes compared to dry pavement
choice_c: They overheat immediately
choice_d: Your wheels may lock up
explanation: When braking hard on slippery surfaces in a vehicle without ABS, the wheels may lock up.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: What happens when a vehicle's steering wheels lock up?
choice_a: You lose steering control
choice_b: The bus accelerates automatically
choice_c: ABS engages regardless of equipment
choice_d: Nothing; steering is unaffected
explanation: When your steering wheels lock up, you lose steering control.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: What does ABS primarily help a driver do?
choice_a: Drive at higher speeds safely in all conditions
choice_b: Avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control, so the driver can steer around an obstacle while braking
choice_c: Eliminate the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_d: Stop instantly regardless of speed or surface
explanation: ABS helps drivers avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control, allowing them to steer around an obstacle while braking and avoid skids caused by over braking.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: When driving a vehicle with ABS, how should the driver brake under normal circumstances?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_b: Use only the parking brake
choice_c: Avoid braking until the last possible moment, then brake hard
choice_d: Brake as you always have
explanation: When you drive a vehicle with ABS, you should brake as you always have.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: In emergency braking on a bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver NOT do?
choice_a: Pump the brakes
choice_b: Use only the necessary braking force
choice_c: Stay in control of the vehicle
choice_d: Monitor the bus as it slows
explanation: In emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: As the bus slows down, what should the driver do if it is safe to do so, to stay in control?
choice_a: Release the brakes completely at once
choice_b: Monitor the bus and back off the brakes
choice_c: Accelerate slightly to maintain momentum
choice_d: Turn sharply to test the steering response
explanation: As you slow down, monitor your bus and back off the brakes, if it is safe to do so, to stay in control.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If a vehicle does not have ABS, what brake functions does the driver still have?
choice_a: None; the brakes are disabled without ABS
choice_b: Only the parking brake
choice_c: Normal brake functions; drive and brake as you always have
choice_d: Only emergency braking capability
explanation: Without ABS, the driver still has normal brake functions and should drive and brake as always.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If the yellow ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on once the bus is under way, what might this indicate, and what should the driver do?
choice_a: It indicates a fuel problem; refuel immediately
choice_b: It is completely normal and requires no action
choice_c: The parking brake is engaged; release it
choice_d: The driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels; the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally but get the system serviced soon
explanation: If the lamp stays on after the bulb check or comes on while driving, the driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels; the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: Does having ABS mean a driver can follow more closely or drive less carefully?
choice_a: Yes, ABS allows closer following distances
choice_b: Yes, ABS allows less careful driving overall
choice_c: Yes, both closer following and less careful driving are permitted
choice_d: No, ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
explanation: The manual states ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: What types of skids will ABS NOT prevent?
choice_a: Power or turning skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_b: Brake-induced skids only
choice_c: All skids of any kind
choice_d: Skids caused only by worn tires
explanation: ABS should prevent brake-induced skids but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: How does the manual describe ABS in relation to a vehicle's normal brakes and stopping power?
choice_a: As a full replacement for normal brakes
choice_b: As an optional feature with no functional purpose
choice_c: As an "add-on" to your normal brakes, not a replacement for them, that won't increase or decrease ultimate stopping power
choice_d: As a system that overrides normal brakes completely
explanation: ABS is an add-on to your normal brakes, not a replacement for them, and won't increase or decrease ultimate stopping power.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: What does the manual say is the best vehicle safety feature?
choice_a: The antilock braking system
choice_b: The roof-mounted strobe lights
choice_c: The parking brake
choice_d: A safe driver
explanation: The manual states the best vehicle safety feature is still a safe driver.
source_note: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 10 - School Bus, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: When should the overhead roof-mounted white strobe light be used, if the bus is so equipped?
choice_a: When you have limited visibility, meaning you cannot easily see around the bus
choice_b: At all times while the bus is in motion
choice_c: Only during loading and unloading in clear weather
choice_d: Only when requested by a passenger
